can_run <- requireNamespace("weightflow", quietly = TRUE)

## Introduction

The [weightflow](https://jpferreira33.github.io/weightflow/) package by
Juan Pablo Ferreira provides a declarative, pipeable API for survey weight
construction: nonresponse adjustment, calibration (raking, post-stratification,
GREG), trimming, and bootstrap replicate weights.

metasurvey's `step_weight()` integrates weightflow into the step pipeline so
that weight construction becomes a lazy, reproducible step --- just like
`step_compute()` or `step_recode()`. Weights are computed when `bake_steps()`
is called.

## Setup

We simulate a household survey with design weights, demographic variables,
and known population margins.

```{r setup, eval = can_run}
library(metasurvey)
library(weightflow)
library(data.table)

set.seed(2026)
n <- 500

microdata <- data.table(
  id = seq_len(n),
  sex = sample(c("M", "F"), n, replace = TRUE),
  age_grp = sample(c("18-34", "35-54", "55+"), n,
    replace = TRUE,
    prob = c(0.35, 0.40, 0.25)
  ),
  region = sample(c("North", "South", "Central"), n, replace = TRUE),
  income = round(rlnorm(n, log(30000), 0.6)),
  employed = sample(0:1, n, replace = TRUE, prob = c(0.3, 0.7)),
  dw = runif(n, 0.8, 1.5)
)
```

We also define population totals for calibration:

```{r margins, eval = can_run}
pop_sex <- c(M = 120000, F = 125000)
pop_age <- c("18-34" = 80000, "35-54" = 100000, "55+" = 65000)
```

## weightflow standalone

Before integrating with metasurvey, here is the pure weightflow pipeline:

```{r standalone, eval = can_run}
spec <- weighting_spec(microdata, base_weights = dw) |>
  step_calibrate(method = "raking", margins = list(
    sex     = pop_sex,
    age_grp = pop_age
  )) |>
  step_trim_weights(method = "tukey")

prepped <- prep(spec)
summary(prepped)
```

`collect_weights()` returns the data with a `.weight` column:

```{r collect, eval = can_run}
weighted_data <- collect_weights(prepped)
head(weighted_data[, .(id, sex, age_grp, dw, .weight)])
```

## Integration with metasurvey

`step_weight()` wraps the entire weightflow pipeline into a single lazy step.
The weighting specification is stored and executed at `bake_steps()` time.

```{r integration, eval = can_run}
svy <- Survey$new(
  data    = microdata,
  edition = "2023",
  type    = "household",
  psu     = NULL,
  engine  = "data.table",
  weight  = add_weight(annual = "dw")
)

spec <- weighting_spec(microdata, base_weights = dw) |>
  step_calibrate(method = "raking", margins = list(
    sex     = pop_sex,
    age_grp = pop_age
  )) |>
  step_trim_weights(method = "tukey")

svy <- svy |>
  step_weight(spec) |>
  step_compute(high_income = as.integer(income > 50000)) |>
  bake_steps()
```

After baking, the `.weight` column exists and the survey design uses
the calibrated weights:

```{r check-weight, eval = can_run}
head(get_data(svy)[, .(id, dw, .weight, high_income)])
svy$weight
```

## Running estimations

With calibrated weights in place, `workflow()` produces design-consistent
estimates:

```{r workflow, eval = can_run}
results <- workflow(
  list(svy),
  survey::svymean(~income, na.rm = TRUE),
  survey::svymean(~employed, na.rm = TRUE),
  survey::svytotal(~high_income, na.rm = TRUE),
  estimation_type = "annual"
)
print(results)
```

## Custom weight column name

Use `weight_var` to control the output column name:

```{r custom-name, eval = can_run}
svy2 <- Survey$new(
  data    = microdata,
  edition = "2023",
  type    = "household",
  psu     = NULL,
  engine  = "data.table",
  weight  = add_weight(annual = "dw")
)

svy2 <- svy2 |>
  step_weight(spec, weight_var = "calibrated_w") |>
  bake_steps()

"calibrated_w" %in% names(get_data(svy2))
svy2$weight
```

## When to use step_weight

| Scenario | Approach |
|----------|----------|
| Weights already in the microdata | Use `add_weight()` directly |
| Need calibration / nonresponse adjustment | Use `step_weight()` with a weightflow spec |
| Multiple weighting strategies to compare | Create separate specs and surveys |
| Bootstrap replicate weights | Use `weightflow::bootstrap_weights()` then `add_weight()` with replicate spec |
